title: Three identical vortices on a square torus are chaotic
credit: Borisov, Mamaev, Kilin, Regul. Chaotic Dyn. (2019); survey arXiv:2003.00716 (Thm 7); Stremler-Aref (1999, chao-dyn/9907038) for the zero-circulation integrable case
plain: On a flat torus, three point vortices with total circulation zero form an integrable system (Stremler-Aref), but for vortices of equal strength even three are believed chaotic, from numerics only. Prove that three identical point vortices on the square torus are not integrable; the same question is open for four.
math:
Let $\mathbb T=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z)$ and $G$ the Green function of the torus Laplacian ($\Delta G=\delta_0-1$, unique up to an additive constant, which does not affect the dynamics). Three unit vortices $z_1,z_2,z_3\in\mathbb T$ evolve by the Hamiltonian flow of $H=-\sum_{j<k}G(z_j-z_k)$ for the symplectic form $\sum_k dx_k\wedge dy_k$ on the collision-free set $\{z_j
e z_k\}$. By translation invariance the flow descends to the reduced space $M_3=\{z_j
e z_k\}/\mathbb T$ (diagonal translations; equivalently the relative positions $w_1=z_2-z_1$, $w_2=z_3-z_1$ with $w_1,w_2,w_1-w_2
e0$), a 4-manifold with the reduced symplectic structure, on which $H$ is a function. Claim: there is no real-analytic $F:M_3	o\mathbb R$, constant along the reduced flow, with $dF\wedge dH
ot\equiv0$. (Four vortices: the same statement on the 6-dimensional reduced space, asking for no two additional independent commuting integrals, is a separate proposition ClaimN4, not part of Claim.)
